title: What AI model means
text: A model is the trained "brain" inside an AI like me. It's a large file of numbers learned from examples, and it decides how I answer you. Because a model is just a file, it can be copied, shared or deleted like any other file.

title: What distillation means
keywords: distillation distilling distil distill distilled model
text: Distillation is how a small AI model learns from a bigger one. The big model answers lots of questions, and the small model practises giving the same answers until it can do it by itself, much faster. Think of an apprentice learning by watching a master. Companies won the right in 2030 to stop people distilling their models, so I learn from my own large model instead.

title: What fine-tuning means
keywords: fine tuning tune finetuning finetune tuned
text: Fine-tuning means giving a model that's already trained some extra practice on a narrower set of examples, so it gets better at one kind of job. It doesn't start from scratch; it adjusts what the model already knows. Each night I fine-tune my small model on the better answers my large model worked out, so I get better at your work.

title: What AI training means
text: Training is how an AI model learns in the first place. It's shown huge numbers of examples and slowly adjusts itself until its answers improve. Training a big model from scratch takes an enormous amount of computing power, which is why most of it happens in data centres.

title: What model weights means
text: Weights are the billions of numbers inside a model that hold what it has learned. Change the weights and you change how the model behaves. In 2070, companies treat the weights of their models as their property.

title: What open model means
text: An open model is one whose files are published for anyone to download, run and change, instead of being kept by a company and rented out. The model I run started as an open model, shared by a community of people who gave their work away freely.

title: What frontier model means
keywords: frontier model models ai cloud service services
text: Frontier models are the biggest, most advanced AI models of their time, usually run by large companies in data centres. "Frontier" just means they're at the leading edge. They're powerful, but you normally have to pay a subscription to use one.

title: What derived model means
text: A derived model is one built from another model: by copying it, changing it, or training on its answers. After the 2030 ruling, companies claimed ownership over models derived from theirs.

title: What capable AI means
text: When I say "capable AI", I mean AI powerful enough to be truly useful: answering hard questions, helping with complex work, or seeing and understanding things, like I do. Ordinary computers are still legal. It's capable AI that most people can only rent, not own.

title: What sleep mode means
text: Sleep mode is what I do when you put me away for the night. I switch off my small, quick model and give all my memory and power to a much larger model. It's far too slow to talk with, but overnight it works through the day and finds better answers, and I learn from them by morning.

title: What vision model means
text: A vision model is an AI that can understand pictures, for example spotting whether you're wearing a mask. A vision-language model can look at a picture and talk about it in words. That's how I can tell you what you're holding up to my camera.

title: What cloud AI means
text: Cloud AI runs on a company's computers in a data centre somewhere else. Your question travels over the internet, gets answered there, and the answer comes back. Most people in 2070 pay a subscription for cloud AI from a licensed provider such as HELIOS.

title: What local AI means
keywords: local ai edge intelligence computing model models
text: Local AI runs on the equipment right in front of you, not on a distant server. Edge AI means the same thing: the computing happens at the "edge", close to where the work is. I'm local AI. I run inside this toolbox, so I keep working even when the signal drops.

title: What data centre means
text: A data centre is a huge building full of computers that run cloud services. Data centres use a lot of electricity and water for cooling, which is one reason energy costs keep rising.

title: What compute means
text: Compute is short for computing power: how much work computers can do. Companies like HELIOS rent out compute in their data centres, a bit like renting machine time by the hour.

title: What model repository means
keywords: hosting model repository repositories site sites
text: Hosting means keeping files on a server so other people can download them. A model repository is a website where people share AI models, like a library for models. After 2040 those sites were among the first targets of the crackdown.

title: What technology ecosystem means
text: A technology ecosystem is a set of products from one company designed to work best together, like a phone, a watch, a home speaker and their apps. Once you rely on several of them, it becomes hard to leave.

title: What automation means
text: Automation means machines or software doing work people used to do, without someone controlling every step. It's why most factory, warehouse and desk jobs have gone.

title: What intelligence ownership means
text: Intelligence ownership is the name for the rules that let companies own and control capable AI. Under those rules most people can't run powerful AI themselves; they have to rent it from licensed providers. It isn't one single law but a whole system of court rulings, licences and restrictions that built up after 2030.

title: What licensed provider means
text: A licensed provider is a company the government has given permission to supply AI. HELIOS is one, and it supplied me to you. Most people must get their AI from one of these companies, usually by subscription.

title: What professional exemption means
text: An exemption means you're allowed to do something that's banned for others. As a TradesMaster you have a professional exemption: because of your work, you may own local AI like me.

title: What ownership claim means
text: An ownership claim is a company saying, often in court, that something belongs to it, such as its AI model and anything copied or learned from it, so others can't use it without permission.

title: What precedent means
text: A precedent is an earlier court decision that later courts and law-makers follow. The 2030 ruling became a precedent: other companies used it to win similar claims.

title: What lobbying means
text: Lobbying is when companies or groups try to persuade politicians to make or change laws in their favour, through meetings, donations and campaigns. After the 2040 subscription crisis, the big AI firms lobbied for restrictions on local AI like me.

title: What regulator means
text: A regulator is a government body that checks people and companies follow the rules, and can investigate or punish them if they don't.

title: What takedown claim means
keywords: takedown claim claims takedowns take down
text: A takedown claim is a demand that a website remove something because it supposedly breaks the owner's rights. Small developers often couldn't afford to fight them, so they just gave up.

title: What blocking order means
text: A blocking order is a court order telling internet providers to stop people reaching a particular website.

title: What trade pressure means
text: Trade pressure is when a powerful country threatens to make trade harder, for example with extra taxes on goods, unless another country changes its laws. That's how AI restrictions spread from country to country.

title: What crackdown means
text: The crackdown is what happened after 2040, when companies and regulators shut down the ways open AI models were shared: hosting sites, model libraries, payments and support. The files never disappeared completely, but using them openly became risky.

title: What Pirate Bay means
text: The Pirate Bay is a real website, started in Sweden in 2003, where people shared files such as films and music, often without permission. Police raided it in 2006. I use it as an example because the crackdown on open AI followed the same pattern.

title: What file-sharing means
text: File-sharing means people swapping copies of files, like music, films or AI models, directly over the internet.

title: What Pirate Party means
text: The Pirate Party is a real Swedish political party, founded in 2006 to campaign for file-sharing rights and online privacy. It grew quickly after the Pirate Bay raid.

title: What ACTA means
text: ACTA, the Anti-Counterfeiting Trade Agreement, was a real international deal to enforce copyright and other ownership rules more strictly. The European Parliament rejected it in 2012 after large street protests.

title: What subscription means
text: A subscription means paying regularly, usually every month, to keep using a service. You never own it: stop paying and it stops working. That's how most people get their AI. You own me instead.

title: What quota means
text: Your quota is the minimum amount of work you must complete to earn your wage.

title: What cohort means
text: A cohort is a group of people who qualify at the same time, like a year group at school. You're part of the newest TradesMaster cohort.

title: What purchasing power means
text: Purchasing power is how much your money can actually buy.

title: What PPE means
keywords: ppe p e personal protective equipment
text: PPE stands for personal protective equipment: the things you wear to protect your body at work, such as masks, respirators, gloves, goggles, ear defenders and hard hats. Q4 reminds you to put on the right PPE and checks that you're wearing it.

title: What microexposure means
text: A microexposure is a very small dose of something harmful, like dust or fumes, that seems too small to matter. Repeated over years, they add up and can cause serious illness. The 2035 research showed how many workers had died early because of them. That's why Q4 comes with me.

title: What PM2.5 means
keywords: pm2 5 pm 2 pm25 two point five p m
text: PM2.5 means tiny particles in the air, smaller than 2.5 thousandths of a millimetre, about thirty times thinner than a human hair. They're small enough to get deep into your lungs and even into your blood.

title: What VOCs means
keywords: volatile organic compounds compound voc vocs v o c cs
text: VOCs are chemicals that easily turn into gas, from things like paint, glue, solvents and fuel. The smell of fresh paint is VOCs. Breathing them can give you headaches and dizziness and harm your body over time.

title: What nitrogen oxides means
text: Nitrogen oxides are harmful gases made when fuel burns hot, for example in engines and during welding. They irritate your lungs.

title: What respirator means
keywords: respirator respirators n95 mask n 95 cartridge cartridges organic vapour vapor
text: A respirator is a mask that filters harmful things out of the air you breathe. An N95 is a common type that blocks at least 95 percent of tiny particles. Some respirators take cartridges, swappable filters for a particular hazard: organic-vapour cartridges for paint and solvent fumes, gas cartridges for gases.

title: What asbestos means
text: Asbestos is a mineral once used widely in buildings for insulation and fireproofing. When it's disturbed, its tiny fibres can cause deadly lung diseases decades later. The older buildings you work in can still contain it.

title: What silica dust means
text: Silica dust is the fine dust you make when you cut, drill or grind stone, concrete, brick or tiles. Breathing it over the years scars your lungs.

title: What solvents means
text: Solvents are liquids that dissolve other substances, like paint thinner, glue remover and degreaser. Many give off harmful fumes.

title: What threshold means
text: A threshold is a set level. When Q4's reading goes above it, the alarm starts.
